IBM Toolkit level is IBM's staged adoption scale (1 is essential, high-impact requirements); report IBM's result even when it has zero violations, without saying "no automated violations found." Don't convert one scale into the other.
 12. Report computed checks (contrast measured from resolved styles) in their own section. Give the measured ratio next to the ratio the criterion needs, and name the state or the method. Never add them to axe-core or IBM counts. Treat `undetermined` as a gap, never as a pass. When a control has visible text and a pale edge, the result is `not-applicable`, because the text identifies the control. Say that, and leave it for a person to confirm.
 13. Report conditions checks (reduced motion, dark mode, more and less contrast, reduced transparency, forced colors, reflow at 320 pixels, text spacing) in their own section, with the numbers from `results.json`. Never add them to axe-core or IBM counts. "Not applicable" means the page doesn't use the feature, such as a page with no dark theme, so don't list it as a failure or a pass. Say what each check can't see: JavaScript-driven motion, overlapping text, and two-dimensional content that WCAG exempts from reflow.
 14. Say which results come from generated fixtures. A generated fixture is a guess about how the library is assembled, so a failure may come from the wiring and not from the library. Call those results lower evidence than an authored fixture, name the recipe from the **Fixture** column, and don't compare a generated result with an authored one as if they were equal. If the user wants a result to stand on its own, write an authored fixture for it.
 15. When you name a WCAG criterion, use the number and name exactly as `report.md` prints them, and keep its "WCAG data" credit to the W3C. Don't write criterion names or levels from memory.
 16. End with a plain method note. Say what automated tools can't catch: whether alt text is meaningful, whether link and heading text make sense in context, cognitive load, real focus and reading order in use, and how real screen readers behave. Those need a person.
 
 Use the structure of `report.md`. Quote selectors and rule IDs exactly as `results.json` has them.
 Keep `report.md` screenshot links attached to their relevant finding or story when writing a separate summary.
 
 ## 7. When a target can't be tested
 
 Say these things plainly. Don't soften them, and don't fill in a result.
 
 - **Unsupported framework.** The package needs a framework other than React, Vue 3, Angular 22 and newer, Svelte 5 and newer, plain HTML, or web components. Name it, and say which version is unsupported (Vue 2, Svelte 4, or Angular 21, for example). This version covers React, Vue 3, Angular 22 and newer, Svelte 5 and newer, plain HTML, and web components. A Storybook for the library still works, whatever the framework.
 - **Not applicable.** The package has no rendering surface, such as a utility library. There's nothing to test.
 - **Not testable.** The content is a canvas with no alternative, or sits in a closed shadow root. The rule engines can't see it, so the result is untested, not clean. The virtual screen reader also can't read open shadow roots.
 - **Gap.** The archetype has no usable fixture or no matching export. Say what the archetype needs.
 - **Error.** An interaction or computed check couldn't finish. It's untested, not failed.
 - **Undetermined.** A computed check found a gradient, an image, or transparency behind the control, so it can't reduce the page to one color. It's untested, not clean.
 - **Failed target.** The target can't be reached, isn't a web page, or couldn't be built. The tool records it as failed with a reason. Tell the user which target failed, using the reason from `results.json`, including when every target failed during resolution before auditing. Don't retry with guesses. If an npm target failed with a network or install error (for example `ETARGET`), you may run the same command once more. If it fails again, report it. If every target failed (exit code 4), stop. If others ran, report them, and list the failed target as a gap in coverage.
 
 ## 8. Stay out of setup
 
 Anything about installing, configuring, or repairing tools belongs to the tool. If `doctor` doesn't cover it, tell the user what failed and stop.

# pantoken (Instructure design tokens & icons)

When styling this project, use pantoken components, icons and tokens.

- First distinguish a maintained application from a standalone artifact. For a single HTML mockup
  or sendable email, follow the `create-pantoken-mockup` skill instead of scaffolding a project.
- In a shadcn project, discover CSS items with `shadcn search @pantoken`, inspect with `shadcn view
  @pantoken/<item>`, and install with `shadcn add @pantoken/<item>`. These are styles and metadata,
  not React components. `@pantoken/shadcn` is only the CSS-variable bridge.

- Tokens are CSS custom properties `--instui-<group>-<name>` (e.g. `--instui-color-background-brand`).
  Use `var(--instui-*)` references, never hard-coded colours, so theming keeps working. Resolve real
  names from `@pantoken/tokens` — don't guess. If the exact token name is unknown, state that the
  token name must be verified against `@pantoken/tokens` and provide a placeholder like
  `--instui-<group>-<name>` with a comment noting it needs confirmation.
- Web app: `import "@pantoken/css/inject";` to define the properties.
- Icons: `@pantoken/web-components` (`<instui-icon name="…">`) or `@pantoken/react` (`<Icon>`).
- InstUI-look CSS components (no framework dependency): `@pantoken/components`
  (`components.css`, `base.css`, `prose.css`, `utilities.css`, `fonts.css`) — class-based markup
  like `<button class="instui-button">`.
- Component behaviors (vanilla JS): `@pantoken/interactions` (`initModal`, `initTooltip`,
  `initInPlaceEdit`, `initCloseButton`). `initInPlaceEdit` accepts an optional `inputType` hint;
  supported hints are `text`, `number`, `email`, `url`, `tel`, and `search`. Validate its committed
  `change` value in the consuming application.
- ARIA tree-browser markup needs `initTreeBrowser` or `tree-browser.iife.js` for keyboard navigation.
  Name the tree, use focusable treeitems, and associate collection rows with groups via `aria-owns`.
  Native details/summary disclosures can use the CSS without claiming tree roles.
- Give `<instui-drawer-layout>` nonempty `tray-label` and `content-label` attributes to name its
  shadow-DOM regions. Labels on slotted content don't name those panes.
- Native form validation is opt-in through `initFormField(host, control, error)` or
  `data-native-validation` plus `form-field.iife.js`. Supply a separate error with a unique ID.
  CSS alone doesn't synchronize error associations; server-side validation is still required.
- ARIA menu keyboard behavior is opt-in via `initMenu(menu, button)` or `data-menu-navigation`
  plus `menu.iife.js`. Use a vertical, single-level native popover and its button. Applications own
  actions and checked state; disabled items need `aria-disabled`. Submenus and menubars aren't supported.
- Tables can use `-layout-responsive` inside an `instui-container` (load `utilities.css`) for
  CSS-only stacking below the canonical `md` container breakpoint. Match localized `data-label`
  values to column headers; retain native header associations. Alternatively, keep columns in a
  named, keyboard-focusable `--overflow-x-auto` region with a visible focus outline.
- Tailwind: `pantokenPreset()` from `@pantoken/tailwind`.
- Native / CMS/site/design targets: `npx pantoken generate
  <swift|android|compose|flutter|rust|wordpress|vanilla|drupal|swatches|icon-font|pendo|mintlify|jekyll|hugo>`.
- Check the [target compatibility registry](https://pantoken.app/target-compatibility.json) before recommending a host version. Its
  `$schema` field links the schema; tested versions and environments do not imply future support.
- For InstUI React components use `@instructure/ui-*`; pantoken is the token/icon layer. Use
  `@instructure/ui-*` for interactive, accessible UI components (buttons, modals, forms). Use
  `@pantoken/react` only for icons and token consumption. Do not substitute one for the other.

# pantoken

> Instructure UI design tokens and icons, exported once and re-shaped for many platforms — CSS, JS,
> native (Swift/Android/Compose/Flutter), design tools (Figma), and framework integrations. Tokens
> are CSS custom properties named `--instui-*`; icons come from Lucide + Instructure custom glyphs.
>
> Built and used internally at Instructure, then open-sourced without official Instructure
> warranty/support — published under [github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken](https://github.com/thedannywahl/pantoken)
> rather than the `instructure` org for now, not a third party.

## Getting started

- [Unified package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pantoken/pantoken): `npm i @pantoken/pantoken` — every target under one import; subpaths like `@pantoken/pantoken/css`, `@pantoken/pantoken/react`, `@pantoken/pantoken/tailwind`.
- Ready-made styled components (plain HTML/CSS): `@pantoken/components` — `components.css`, `base.css`,
	`utilities.css`, `prose.css`. Pair with `@pantoken/plugin-layouts` (app-shell layout) and
	`@pantoken/plugin-custom-components` (additional components like `banner` and `agent-shell`). Card is included in `@pantoken/components`.
- Web CSS from raw tokens (no components): `@pantoken/css` — `import "@pantoken/css/inject"` defines all `--instui-*` properties.
- Tokens as data: `@pantoken/tokens` — `import { tokens, byTheme } from "@pantoken/tokens"`.
- Icons: `@pantoken/icons` for raw decoded SVG markup/data (`getIcon("arrow-left")`), or
	`@pantoken/web-components` for a drop-in `<instui-icon>` custom element.
- Component behaviors (vanilla JS): `@pantoken/interactions` — `initModal`, `initTooltip`,
	`initInPlaceEdit`, `initCloseButton`; IIFE entry points for CDN. `initInPlaceEdit` accepts an
	optional `text`, `number`, `email`, `url`, `tel`, or `search` input hint, but the consuming
	application validates committed values.
- Tree browser: ARIA tree markup needs `initTreeBrowser` or `tree-browser.iife.js` for keyboard
	navigation. Name the tree, use focusable treeitems, and associate collection rows with groups via
	`aria-owns`. CSS-only details/summary disclosures don't claim tree roles.
- Drawer layout: give `<instui-drawer-layout>` nonempty `tray-label` and `content-label`
	attributes to name its shadow-DOM regions. Labels on slotted content don't name those panes.
- Form validation: opt into `initFormField(host, control, error)` or `data-native-validation` plus
	`form-field.iife.js`, with a separate error and unique ID. CSS alone doesn't synchronize error
	associations; client-side checks don't replace server validation.
- Menus: opt into `initMenu(menu, button)` or `data-menu-navigation` plus `menu.iife.js` for
	vertical, single-level native popover menus. Applications own actions and checked state;
	disabled items need `aria-disabled`. Submenus and menubars aren't supported.
- Tables: `-layout-responsive` inside an `instui-container` (with `utilities.css`) stacks below
	the canonical `md` container breakpoint without JavaScript. Match localized `data-label` values
	to column headers and retain native header associations. Alternatively, retain columns in a
	named, keyboard-focusable `--overflow-x-auto` region with a visible focus outline.
- shadcn registry: `shadcn search @pantoken`, `shadcn view @pantoken/<item>`, then `shadcn add
	@pantoken/<item>`. Items install CSS/packages and usage metadata, not React components.
- Standalone browser mockups: use the CDN guide, component capability manifest, demos, and optional
	per-component interaction IIFEs. Sendable email uses `@pantoken/email` `inlineEmailHtml` or
	`pantoken generate email`; generic HTML/CSS inlining uses `@pantoken/inline-styles` or
	`pantoken generate inline`.

## Frameworks

- React: `@pantoken/react` · Vue: `@pantoken/vue` · Svelte: `@pantoken/svelte` · Angular: `@pantoken/angular` · React Native: `@pantoken/react-native`
- Markdown: `@pantoken/react-markdown`, `@pantoken/rehype`

## Build tools

- `@pantoken/vite` · `@pantoken/next` · `@pantoken/webpack` · `@pantoken/tailwind` · `@pantoken/postcss`

## Theming other systems

- `@pantoken/shadcn` · `@pantoken/bootstrap` · `@pantoken/storybook`

## Native & other ecosystems (CLI: `pantoken generate <target>`)

- swift, android, compose, flutter, rust, wordpress, vanilla, drupal, jekyll, hugo — add
	`--icons`, `--theme`, `--out`, and for rust `--format`.
- Check https://pantoken.app/target-compatibility.json before claiming a supported host version;
	its `$schema` field identifies the published schema. Verified releases and environments are
	bounded evidence, not promises about newer versions.

## AI tooling for consumers

- `@pantoken/ai` provides installable agent assets: `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt`, and editor/assistant
	rules for Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, and Claude Code.
- CLI: `npx pantoken-ai init [--tool <all|agents|llms|cursor|copilot|windsurf|claude>] [--dir <path>]`.

## Design & interchange

- `@pantoken/dtcg` (W3C DTCG JSON) · `@pantoken/scss` · `@pantoken/figma` (Figma Variables) · `@pantoken/email`

## Conventions

- Token names: `--instui-<group>-<name>` (e.g. `--instui-color-background-brand`).
- Themes: rebrand (default), canvas, canvasHighContrast. Prefer `var(--instui-*)` references for theming.

 	`utilities.css`, `prose.css`. Pair with `@pantoken/plugin-layouts` (app-shell layout) and
 	`@pantoken/plugin-custom-components` (additional components like `banner` and `agent-shell`). Card is included in `@pantoken/components`.
 - Web CSS from raw tokens (no components): `@pantoken/css` — `import "@pantoken/css/inject"` defines all `--instui-*` properties.
 - Tokens as data: `@pantoken/tokens` — `import { tokens, byTheme } from "@pantoken/tokens"`.
 - Icons: `@pantoken/icons` for raw decoded SVG markup/data (`getIcon("arrow-left")`), or
 	`@pantoken/web-components` for a drop-in `<instui-icon>` custom element.
 - Component behaviors (vanilla JS): `@pantoken/interactions` — `initModal`, `initTooltip`,
 	`initInPlaceEdit`, `initCloseButton`; IIFE entry points for CDN. `initInPlaceEdit` accepts an
 	optional `text`, `number`, `email`, `url`, `tel`, or `search` input hint, but the consuming
 	application validates committed values.
 - Tree browser: ARIA tree markup needs `initTreeBrowser` or `tree-browser.iife.js` for keyboard
 	navigation. Name the tree, use focusable treeitems, and associate collection rows with groups via
 	`aria-owns`. CSS-only details/summary disclosures don't claim tree roles.
 - Drawer layout: give `<instui-drawer-layout>` nonempty `tray-label` and `content-label`
 	attributes to name its shadow-DOM regions. Labels on slotted content don't name those panes.
 - Form validation: opt into `initFormField(host, control, error)` or `data-native-validation` plus
 	`form-field.iife.js`, with a separate error and unique ID. CSS alone doesn't synchronize error
 	associations; client-side checks don't replace server validation.
 - Menus: opt into `initMenu(menu, button)` or `data-menu-navigation` plus `menu.iife.js` for
 	vertical, single-level native popover menus. Applications own actions and checked state;
 	disabled items need `aria-disabled`. Submenus and menubars aren't supported.
 - Tables: `-layout-responsive` inside an `instui-container` (with `utilities.css`) stacks below
 	the canonical `md` container breakpoint without JavaScript. Match localized `data-label` values
 	to column headers and retain native header associations. Alternatively, retain columns in a
 	named, keyboard-focusable `--overflow-x-auto` region with a visible focus outline.
 - shadcn registry: `shadcn search @pantoken`, `shadcn view @pantoken/<item>`, then `shadcn add
 	@pantoken/<item>`. Items install CSS/packages and usage metadata, not React components.
 - Standalone browser mockups: use the CDN guide, component capability manifest, demos, and optional
 	per-component interaction IIFEs. Sendable email uses `@pantoken/email` `inlineEmailHtml` or
 	`pantoken generate email`; generic HTML/CSS inlining uses `@pantoken/inline-styles` or
 	`pantoken generate inline`.
 
 ## Frameworks
 
 - React: `@pantoken/react` · Vue: `@pantoken/vue` · Svelte: `@pantoken/svelte` · Angular: `@pantoken/angular` · React Native: `@pantoken/react-native`
 - Markdown: `@pantoken/react-markdown`, `@pantoken/rehype`
 
 ## Build tools
 
 - `@pantoken/vite` · `@pantoken/next` · `@pantoken/webpack` · `@pantoken/tailwind` · `@pantoken/postcss`
 
 ## Theming other systems
 
 - `@pantoken/shadcn` · `@pantoken/bootstrap` · `@pantoken/storybook`
 
 ## Native & other ecosystems (CLI: `pantoken generate <target>`)
 
 - swift, android, compose, flutter, rust, wordpress, vanilla, drupal, jekyll, hugo — add
 	`--icons`, `--theme`, `--out`, and for rust `--format`.
 - Check https://pantoken.app/target-compatibility.json before claiming a supported host version;
 	its `$schema` field identifies the published schema. Verified releases and environments are
 	bounded evidence, not promises about newer versions.
 
 ## AI tooling for consumers
 
 - `@pantoken/ai` provides installable agent assets: `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt`, and editor/assistant
 	rules for Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf, and Claude Code.
 - CLI: `npx pantoken-ai init [--tool <all|agents|llms|cursor|copilot|windsurf|claude>] [--dir <path>]`.
 
 ## Design & interchange
 
 - `@pantoken/dtcg` (W3C DTCG JSON) · `@pantoken/scss` · `@pantoken/figma` (Figma Variables) · `@pantoken/email`
 
 ## Conventions
 
 - Token names: `--instui-<group>-<name>` (e.g. `--instui-color-background-brand`).
 - Themes: rebrand (default), canvas, canvasHighContrast. Prefer `var(--instui-*)` references for theming.

CSS. Each documented record is one file; the bucket `index.ts` is a barrel + registry, not a monolith.

User preferences are intrinsic behavior, not modifiers. Gate decorative transitions and animations

don't smooth-scroll, delay removal for a skipped fade, or hide progress behind a mount animation.
Do not shorten loading timeouts or cancel announcements in the name of reducing motion.

**Exploring dark mode emulation**

I’m considering how the native checkbox default should inherit color in a forced dark mode. The computed color for a checkbox is typically black, but I wonder if it should change under a dark theme? If I'm emulating this in Chrome, I can use `page.emulateMedia`. It's interesting that the forced color scheme could affect how the canvas displays, especially since the CSS root might override settings. I need to test this with both light and dark settings to see how they interact!

**Evaluating screenshot testing**

I'm thinking about how to measure the pixel count of an icon versus the actual colors used on the surface. I can get the computed colors, but those don’t always show the true colors if the glyph is blocked by the source rendering. It feels like a challenge to determine the actual visual representation. So, taking a screenshot to analyze pixel count seems necessary to ensure I'm getting accurate data on the used colors.

## Automatic user preferences

User preferences are intrinsic behavior, not modifiers. Gate decorative transitions and animations
with `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` in each record so standalone sheets and shadow styles
follow the same policy. Keep loading and progress indicators visible when animation stops, and
apply state changes immediately. Interaction behaviors must also respect the live preference:
don't smooth-scroll, delay removal for a skipped fade, or hide progress behind a mount animation.
Do not shorten loading timeouts or cancel announcements in the name of reducing motion.

Token sheets handle color preferences in the active theme's scope. `prefers-contrast: more`
strengthens nonzero border widths and focus rings; `less` removes decorative elevation color without
reducing text contrast. Keep semantic text/status colors and explicit light/dark pins intact.
Links gain an underline in more-contrast mode, including normally unstyled links.

Reduced transparency composites translucent surface tokens over an opaque semantic background.
Remove backdrop blur in that mode, and use opaque muted colors rather than whole-control opacity for
disabled states. Keep intentionally empty backgrounds, image effects, and visibility transitions:
they aren't interchangeable with translucent component chrome. New surface expressions need coverage
in the token preference generator and a real-browser check.

## Source layout

- `src/components/<name>/index.ts` + `<name>.css` (`COMPONENTS` registry).
- `src/components/<name>/members/<member>/index.ts` + `<member>.css` — a promoted sub-component (see
  "Sub-components (`@memberOf`)" below).
- `src/utilities/<name>/index.ts` + `<name>.css` (`UTILITIES`).
- `src/rules/{base,prose}/index.ts` + `<name>.css` (`RULES`).
- `src/declarations/<name>/index.ts` + `<name>.css` (`DECLARATIONS`).

data.summaryContent:
<overview>
The user wants automatica11y integrated as a dev tool for `formats/components`, followed by accessibility remediation in incremental conventional commits, each with Changesets and tests. The scope expanded to automatic library-wide preference handling—motion, contrast, transparency, color scheme, and forced colors—without enabling classes or variants. Two new preference increments are committed; a third forced-colors/native-progress increment is in progress, and a complete audit is still running.
</overview>

<history>
1. **Original integration and release discipline**
   - User: “I want to add automatica11y from npm as a dev tool for auditing the css in formats/components.”
   - User: “work in incremental conventional commits with changesets and test coverage.”
   - Added authored fixtures, rendered-page/npm audits, advisory CI artifacts, and runner coverage.
   - Scope: 456 page targets (76 examples × six theme/scheme combinations), plus 54 npm targets; 510 targets / 540 configurations total.
   - Tool/settings: automatica11y 0.11.0, WCAG 2.2 AA, axe-core and IBM Equal Access, three themes × light/dark.

2. **Concurrency, Actions, and Snyk**
   - Explained that `gh` dispatches/inspects hosted Actions, rather than executing them locally.
   - Shared Vitest `maxWorkers: 2`, tests, and docs committed as `33739d868`.
   - At that time, `vp run ready` passed 179 tasks and 3,243 tests.
   - Hosted pantoken run 40562948018 succeeded, but predates remediation.
   - Snyk CLI is available, but no scan has run: standard Snyk Code uploads source, prohibited by environment constraints. No approved local/on-prem endpoint or permitted scan tool was found. Security verification remains pending.

3. **Remediation steps 0–3**
   - User requested a remediation plan while CI ran, then: “start with 0, and let me know when it's done, then move one.”
   - Step 0 corrected per-state coverage accounting; original reports remain immutable.
   - Step 1 fixed tree-browser semantics/keyboard behavior, native number-input keyboard ownership, drawer naming, radio-group names, and opt-in native validation.
   - Checkbox simulator flag was identified as an exact-role-word heuristic; genuine accessible labels were preserved.
   - Step 2 fixed modal native activation order.
   - Step 3 added opt-in ARIA menu behavior and fixed contrast/native paint.
   - User explicitly deferred translation synchronization. Old drift counts are stale.

4. **Tooltip and responsive fixes**
   - User chose progressively enhanced tooltip behavior: CSS-only fallback, initialized JS owns visibility/dismissal.
   - Escape latch, independent focus/pointer reasons, viewport fitting, and bounded pointer corridor were implemented.
   - Tooltip commits: `289c699ff`, `9a64bdc8a`; all original tooltip Escape/reachability/reflow checks passed.
   - Pill example wrapping fixed in `eb91384f4`.
   - Drawer scoped minimum-width reset fixed in `a52918e85`.
   - Responsive tables added in `e2f88416d`, following the user’s choice of both container-based stacking and accessible horizontal scroll regions.
   - Shared forced-colors resting/focused outline distinction fixed in `ed3ed1b40`.
   - All 42 table configurations passed reflow, spacing, and forced-colors focus; substantial browser geometry/keyboard checks passed.

5. **Avatar and initial motion**
   - Avatar clipping was measured under exact WCAG text-spacing overrides. Visible leading glyphs and full accessibility names remained unchanged.
   - Preserved six raw avatar failures as manual-review candidates, rather than suppressing them or relabeling them passes.
   - Guidance/tests committed as `e88421cbb`.
   - Initial spinner/disclosure/mask reduced-motion handling committed as `0a5207537`.
   - All 24 original motion checks passed.

6. **Expanded requirement**
   - User: “the `prefers` set should be inherent in all components - it shouldn't be opt-in or variants. reduced motion, contrast, color-scheme, etc.”
   - User confirmed scheme precedence: **follow system by default; preserve explicit light/dark subtree pins**.
   - User: “continue with the expanded library-wide preference work. and any other issues.”
   - This superseded the earlier deferral of reduced transparency.
   - Full pre-expansion report: `a11y-report/2026-10-28T00-49-41.270Z/index.md`.
     - Zero axe violations; 88 axe reviews.
     - Zero IBM violations; 2,198 IBM reviews.
     - Conditions: 1,506 passes, 2,553 not-applicable, 21 failures.
     - Interactions: 312 passes, 24 not-applicable, zero failures.
     - Computed: 138 passes, 12 not-applicable.
     - Six simulated VSR flags; 90 coverage notices.
     - Failures: 12 forced-colors focus, six avatar spacing, three reduced transparency.
   - This report is a pre-expansion snapshot, not final verification.

7. **This segment: library-wide motion completed and committed**
   - Commit `ad9052a90 fix(components): honor automatic reduced motion throughout library`.
   - Wrapped all remaining decorative motion declarations in `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`:
     badge, checkbox, radio, tray, popover, tooltip, img, toggle-group, progress, progress-circle, transition utility.
   - Existing spinner, toggle-details, and tree-browser reduced-motion overrides retained.
   - Progress-circle’s initially hidden mount state now applies only without reduced motion.
   - Shared focus transitions stop automatically under reduced motion.
   - New shared interaction helper reads the owning document’s live motion query.
   - Smooth scrolling becomes instant under reduction.
   - Removal skips fade waits, and finishes an in-progress fade if preference changes.
   - Progress-circle mount delays release immediately under reduction, including live changes; cleanup detaches listeners.
   - New motion inventory and lifecycle tests, authoring guidance, CLI-generated Changeset.
   - 331 targeted regression tests passed.
   - Coverage sample: 91.7% statements / 96.5% lines over shared motion/lifecycle code before adding the detached-document helper test.
   - 18 real-browser cases passed across all themes/schemes and default → reduce → restored, including shadow spinner.
   - Authored CSS passed stylelint/cssdoc; code passed focused format/lint/type checks and commit hooks.

8. **This segment: contrast choice and automatic color preferences committed**
   - Asked the user one design fork.
   - User selected: **“Preserve palette; adjust boundaries and decoration (recommended)”**.
   - Policy:
     - More contrast: nonzero token borders ≥2px; focus rings ≥3px; links/breadcrumbs get underlines.
     - Less contrast: decorative shadow colors become transparent; no lowering text contrast.
     - Reduced transparency: translucent surface colors composite against opaque semantic surfaces, preserving tint/brand references.
     - Disabled controls use opaque muted text rather than whole-control opacity.
     - Masks/modal backdrops disable blur.
     - System scheme follows automatically from token sheets; defaults live below explicit scheme pins.
   - Localized remaining report failures:
     - Forced-colors focus: range slider’s shadow-only thumb ring, with `outline: none`.
     - Transparency: rebrand tag and number-input arrow surfaces.
   - Range slider now gets a system `Highlight` outline in forced colors.
   - Browser testing uncovered a genuine nested-theme alias bug: nested Canvas tag inherited rebrand’s already-computed alias.
   - Scope partitioning now compares authored values **and resolved dependency signatures**, so theme-dependent aliases are declared locally.
   - Persistent manual scoping fixture gained a regression check.
   - Commit `be10712f6 fix(components): apply automatic color and surface preferences`.
   - Includes CSS preferences generator, scoped alias fix, component styles/tests, demos, docs, AI/scaffold guidance, Changeset.
   - Tests:
     - CSS package: 40 tests passed.
     - Targeted combined color tests: 49 passed.
     - Broader components/utilities: 156 passed.
     - AI installed assets: 12 passed.
     - Generator coverage: 97.72% statements, 97.43% branches, 100% functions/lines.
     - 144 real-browser preference cases passed, with/without optional base reset, across all themes/schemes, live more/less/transparency restoration.
     - Explicit root pins and shadow inheritance passed.
     - All nine persistent scoping browser checks passed.
   - Commit hooks passed.

9. **This segment: full audit launched; forced-colors increment underway**
   - Started:
     ```sh
     vp run @pantoken/components#audit:accessibility
     ```

## Preference generator architecture
`formats/css/src/preferences.ts`:
- `systemSchemeCss()` declares layer order and:
  ```css
  @layer pantoken.base {
    :where(:root) { color-scheme: light dark; }
  }
  ```
- `tokenPreferenceCss(tokens, scope, layer?)`:
  - More: `max(2px, original)` for border-width/border-size tokens, `max(3px, original)` for focus widths.
  - Uses resolver to preserve authored zero-width borders.
  - Less: `--instui-color-drop-shadow-*` becomes transparent.
  - Transparency:
    - Walks only background-related tokens.
    - Recursively follows known `var(--...)` references.
    - Keeps solid references intact; expands only chains requiring compositing.
    - Replaces transparent in `color-mix` with semantic base.
    - Converts partial rgba and 8-digit hex alpha to opaque color-mix.
    - Preserves fully transparent/opaque colors, intentional empty backgrounds, foreground colors, unknown external refs.
    - Cycles throw explicit error.
    - On-color surfaces composite over brand; inverse/dark overlay over inverse; others over base.
  - Media overrides use the same scope/layer as normal declarations.
- `toCss()` emits policies for InstUI tokens automatically on all/declarations paths, never property-only.
- `multiScopeCss()` appends full-token-graph preference overrides per theme because varying-only partitions may omit needed references. Some smaller policy blocks are emitted twice, but full-graph blocks are authoritative; correctness verified.
- No new runtime Node imports; generator uses existing utils.


The user requires preference handling to be inherent in every applicable component, not an
opt-in, new variant, or follow-up opaque-mode feature. The previously targeted fixes aren't
evidence that the whole library has this policy yet.

- Honor reduced motion, increased/reduced contrast, system color scheme, reduced transparency,
